risks.note: Tariff-related measures caused India's gems and jewellery exports to the United States to fall 45% to US$ 5.09 billion during the year; the US is described as one of the industry's most consequential consumer markets, and tariff uncertainty continued to constrain order visibility for Indian exporters.

The company's own commentary flags the cost of concentration in a single export market or logistics corridor as a key vulnerability exposed by FY26 events, reinforcing the need to broaden the market base.

Escalating tensions involving Iran, Israel and the United States caused flight cancellations, airspace closures and interruptions in Dubai-linked cargo movement, affecting both exports and rough diamond imports given Dubai's role as a major hub for polished diamonds, rough diamonds and bullion.

Sustained softness in polished diamond prices and subdued demand in key overseas markets (with the US and China as the most consequential demand variables) pressured the diamond segment; cut and polished diamond exports from India declined 8.52% during the year.
risks.risk: Diamond segment pricing and demand pressure

risks.note: Steep price compression in lab-grown diamonds sharpens consumer comparison across diamond categories, reinforcing the risk that natural diamonds must be differentiated on rarity, origin and traceability to retain value perception.

Unprecedented gold price levels and broader commodity volatility weighed on jewellery consumption (global gold jewellery volumes declined 18% in 2025) and on the company's domestic sales, where elevated gold prices and cautious consumer sentiment weighed on spending.

The WTO projected a slowdown in global goods trade growth from 4.6% (2025) to 1.9% (2026), with tariff effects, geopolitical risks and transport disruptions cited as weighing on the medium-term outlook relevant to an export-oriented business.
